title: Basic Task Execution
description:
This example demonstrates how to create and execute distributed tasks using Blazing Flow.
You'll learn how to:
- Initialize a Blazing Flow application
- Define steps and workflows
- Execute workflows with `app.run()` or direct invocation
- Wait for results with `.wait_result()`
- Proper resource cleanup

title: Connector Integration Patterns
description:
This example demonstrates the connector pattern used in production Blazing
applications. Connectors provide a standardized way to interact with external
services (REST APIs, databases, etc.) with built-in features:

- Connection pooling
- Throttling and rate limiting
- Authentication management
- Health checks

**Pattern:**
1. Define connector configurations
2. Create a service that receives connector_instances
3. Service methods use connectors to access external resources

title: Modular Registration Pattern
description:
This example demonstrates how to organize large Blazing applications using
the modular registration pattern. Instead of defining all steps and workflows
in a single file, you can split them into domain-specific modules.

**Pattern:**
```python
# In main.py:
app = Blazing(...)
register_trading_module(app)
register_analytics_module(app)
register_reporting_module(app)
await app.publish()
```

**Benefits:**
- Clean separation of concerns
- Domain-driven design
- Easy to test individual modules
- Scalable codebase organization
- Conditional feature registration

title: Trading Strategy Sandbox
description:
This example shows how to build a trading strategy platform with two sides:

**YOUR SIDE (Platform Owner):**
- Define services your users can access (MarketDataService)
- Define a workflow that uses run_sandboxed() to execute user code
- Register with Blazing and publish

**YOUR USER'S SIDE (End Users):**
- Write strategy functions using your services
- Submit code as a string
- Get results back safely

**Security Model (5 Layers - ALL HANDLED BY run_sandboxed()):**
1. AST validation - blocks dangerous imports/builtins
2. Cryptographic signing - HMAC-SHA256 prevents tampering
3. Signature verification - server validates before execution
4. Bytecode validation - blocks dangerous opcodes
5. Pyodide WASM sandbox - no network/filesystem access

title: API Execution Patterns
description: Demonstrates three equivalent patterns for invoking workflows and retrieving results: wait_result() one-liner, handle.result() for deferred fetch, and run() by name for string-based dispatch.

title: Decorators and Context Manager
description: Demonstrates how to register steps, workflows, and services using decorators, then use the async context manager (async with app:) to cleanly manage service lifecycle and cleanup.

title: Direct Function Call

title: run_sync by Name

title: SyncBlazing Quickstart

title: wait_result_sync Helper
description: Shows how to use wait_result_sync() on a workflow execution handle for blocking result retrieval in synchronous contexts — useful when mixing sync and async code in the same application.

title: Workflow Handle wait()/cancel()
description: Demonstrates handle lifecycle methods: handle.wait() to block until completion, handle.wait_result() to retrieve the return value, and handle.cancel() to abort an in-flight workflow execution.

title: Workflow Version Pins

title: Depth Across Boundaries
description: Demonstrates a sandboxed step calling a trusted service in the same workflow — a cross-boundary pattern where Pyodide-isolated code accesses a trusted service via the services= injection mechanism.

title: Depth Metrics API
description: Shows how to query the GET /v1/metrics/depth HTTP endpoint after running a workflow to retrieve operations_scanned and other depth statistics for monitoring step execution depth — uses HTTPX.

title: Depth Statistics Metrics
description: Demonstrates querying depth statistics (max_depth, avg_depth, depth_distribution) from the Blazing metrics API after running workflows to understand step nesting patterns — uses HTTPX.

title: Depth Tracking Basics
description: Creates a simple parent workflow calling a single child step to demonstrate Blazing's depth tracking — how the system records parent-child relationships between workflow and step executions.

title: Depth Tracking Chain
description: Builds a chain of three steps where each calls the previous (step_c → step_b → step_a) to demonstrate how Blazing tracks and records multi-level step depth across a call chain.

title: Mixed Executor Routing
description: Routes trusted and sandboxed steps to different executors within one workflow — trusted NON-BLOCKING steps run in the main executor while sandboxed NON-BLOCKING steps run in Pyodide isolation.

title: Mixed Load Profile
description: Blends a CPU-bound BLOCKING step and an async I/O-bound step in a single workflow using asyncio.gather, demonstrating how Blazing routes different load profiles to appropriate executor pools.

title: State Machine Loop
description: Implements a workflow-driven state machine using a while loop — each iteration calls a step that advances the state until a terminal condition is reached, demonstrating looping patterns in Blazing.

title: Worker Type Isolation
description: Demonstrates behavior differences between trusted and sandboxed NON-BLOCKING workers by running the same input through both and comparing results — trusted steps run in the main process, sandboxed in Pyodide.

title: Worker Types Overview
description: Runs all four worker type combinations — trusted BLOCKING, trusted NON-BLOCKING, sandboxed BLOCKING, and sandboxed NON-BLOCKING — in one workflow to demonstrate how step_type and sandboxed flags control executor routing.

title: Worker Types with Services
description: One workflow, four worker types — trusted sync (BLOCKING), trusted async (NON_BLOCKING), and two sandboxed async (NON_BLOCKING_SANDBOXED) steps all calling the same MathOpsService, demonstrating that services['Name'] works identically across all executors.

title: Dynamic Code Execution (Sandboxed)
description: Executes a user-submitted expression string inside a sandboxed step with restricted builtins, demonstrating how to safely evaluate dynamic code while preventing access to dangerous Python built-in functions.

title: Dynamic Code Security
description: Execute user-submitted functions through a 5-layer security pipeline: AST validation, HMAC signing, signature verification, bytecode inspection, and Pyodide sandbox isolation.

title: Egress Policy
description: Declare outbound network rules on services — exact hostnames, wildcard subdomains, CIDR blocks, or deny-all — uses HTTPX.

title: Isolated Execution
description: Runs a compute step inside the Pyodide WASM sandbox using @app.step(sandboxed=True), isolating the workload from the main executor process while still returning results to the workflow.

title: Isolated Execution with Retry
description: Demonstrates retry logic around sandboxed workloads using a try/except loop — if the sandboxed step raises an exception, the workflow waits and retries up to three times before propagating the error.

title: Pyodide Sandbox Dependencies
description: Shows how to install extra Python packages into the Pyodide sandbox using the sandbox_dependencies=['numpy'] parameter, making them available inside sandboxed steps without exposing them to trusted workers.

title: Pyodide Parallel Stress
description: Fires five sandboxed compute tasks simultaneously using asyncio.gather to stress the Pyodide sandbox executor, demonstrating concurrent sandbox execution and verifying that all tasks complete correctly under parallel load.

title: Sandboxed Step Basics
description: The simplest sandboxed step example: marks a step with @app.step(sandboxed=True) to run it in Pyodide WASM isolation, demonstrating the minimal configuration needed for sandbox execution.

title: Tetris2 on Akash
description: Deploy the classic Tetris2 game on Akash decentralized cloud. Uses reverse-auction pricing with a max bid of $15/month. Single region (akash-global) with public HTTP ingress on port 80.

title: Tetris2 on DFC
description: Deploy the classic Tetris2 game on DFC (Digital Frontier Cloud). DFC uses Akash blockchain infrastructure underneath with fixed Spot pricing. Region: dfc-pt-lisbon (Lisbon, Portugal). Cost tab displays BASE/PEAK/SAVINGS columns.

title: Tetris2 on GCP
description: Deploy the classic Tetris2 game on Google Cloud Platform. Uses GCP Standard network tier with fixed pricing in the europe-west1 region. Cost tab displays BASE/PEAK/SAVINGS columns.

title: Tetris2 on GCP Spot
description: Deploy the classic Tetris2 game on GCP using spot (preemptible) instances for 60-90% cost savings. Baseline replica runs on standard on-demand nodes for reliability; burst replicas scale onto spot nodes. Cost tab displays spot rate pricing ($0.0472/core/hr).

title: Tetris2 Multi-Provider
description: Deploy the classic Tetris2 game across 3 providers simultaneously: Akash (global, reverse-auction), GCP (europe-west1, fixed pricing), and DFC (Lisbon, Akash infrastructure). Demonstrates multi-cloud deployment with mixed pricing models in a single cluster.
